name: Nadi Shodhana Pranayama
cardiovascular_benefit: Activates parasympathetic nervous system; reduces sympathetic tone. Clinically shown to reduce systolic BP by 5–15 mmHg in hypertensive patients.
steps: Sit comfortably in Sukhasana or on a chair with spine erect.
Rest left hand on left knee (palm upward in Chin Mudra).
Use right hand Vishnu Mudra: fold index and middle fingers.
Close right nostril with thumb. Inhale through left nostril for 4 counts.
Close both nostrils. Hold for 4 counts (Kumbhaka).
Release right nostril. Exhale for 8 counts through right nostril.
Inhale through right nostril for 4 counts.
Close both nostrils. Hold for 4 counts.
Exhale through left nostril for 8 counts.
This completes one cycle. Perform 10–15 cycles.
contraindications: Do not force retention if uncomfortable

name: Sukhasana with Deep Diaphragmatic Breathing
cardiovascular_benefit: Reduces peripheral vascular resistance. Diaphragmatic breathing stimulates baroreceptors, lowering heart rate and diastolic pressure.
steps: Sit cross-legged on mat. Place hands on knees, palms facing up.
Close eyes. Lengthen spine without rigidity.
Place one hand on chest, one on abdomen.
Inhale slowly through nose for 4 counts – abdomen should rise, chest stays still.
Pause for 1 count at top of breath.
Exhale through mouth with slight pursing for 6–8 counts.
Focus on the abdominal rise and fall exclusively.
Maintain for 15 minutes. Heart rate should decrease within 5 minutes.

name: Viparita Karani (Legs-Up-The-Wall Pose)
cardiovascular_benefit: Promotes venous return; reduces cardiac preload. Gravitational redistribution of blood reduces systolic workload. Evidence-based for acute BP reduction.
steps: Place mat near a wall.
Sit sideways close to the wall, then swing legs up as you lie back.
Rest shoulders and head flat on floor. Arms relaxed by sides.
Legs rest vertically against wall at 90-degree angle.
Close eyes. Breathe naturally.
Remain in pose for 8–10 minutes.
To exit: bend knees, roll gently to one side before sitting up.
